originalTitle: Loot boxes, influencers, and addictive features face an EU crackdown
summary: Gaming, social media, and e-commerce platforms are facing a fresh wave of sweeping European Union rules that aim to make "your online experience fairer." content: Gaming, social media, and e-commerce platforms are facing a fresh wave of sweeping European Union rules that aim to make “your online experience fairer.” The newly proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA) published by the EU Commission on Wednesday is designed to tackle practices that exploit consumers into spending more of their time and money online, including misleading prices or availability, addictive design features like gaming loot boxes, undisclosed influencer marketing, and more. “The Act will protect consumers of all ages shopping and browsing for goods or services online,” the EU Commission said in a news bulletin. “It will also mean fairer competition for businesses, which are expecting to save EU consumers up to €13.7 billion ($15.1 billion) a year.” Here’s an overview of what the DFA proposal includes: * A ban on manipulative marketing practices and so-called “dark patterns” that push consumers into making decisions they might not otherwise make, such as fake claims about a product almost being sold out. * A requirement to give consumers the choice to turn off addictive features, such as persistent prompts, endless scrolling, and autoplay of videos. Restrictions around addictive design also apply to “AI companions and general conversational chatbots.” * Restrictions on unfair practices that encourage overspending, such as banning gambling-like features (pay-to-win and pay-to-progress, for example) for minors. * Requiring influencers to clearly disclose advertising content, and restrictions to prevent them from exploiting the trust of children. * Restrictions on unfair personalised ads and prices that target minors or take advantage of sensitive data. * Making subscriptions and digital contracts easier to cancel, with prompts to remind customers about upcoming automatic renewals and free trial periods coming to an end. * Requiring clear and transparent pricing, especially around dynamic pricing and purchases using virtual in-app currency. When consumers wait in virtual queues for cultural and sports event tickets, companies will have to show the current price in real time and at the highest possible price. * Giving consumers the right to communicate with a human customer service representative, and clear rights using an AI agent to make purchases. The scope of the restrictions being proposed is broad, and could have a significant impact on major parts of the online digital landscape, from the “rabbit hole” algorithms across YouTube, TikTok, and Meta platforms, to AI chatbots and apps like DuoLingo that relentlessly nudge users to keep interacting with them. Some gaming organizations have already slammed the DFA proposal, describing its restrictions around virtual currencies, loot boxes, and offering micro-transactions to minors as being “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate.” Given this is a draft proposal, the DFA will undergo various approvals through the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union before being passed into law, and its current measures could be changed or removed entirely as part of that process. When (or if) it does come into force, the EU Commission says companies who violate the regulations could see fines of up to six percent of their worldwide annual turnover. “Our consumer protection rules will help ensure that businesses compete on the merits of their products and services - not on their ability to exploit consumers or evade the rules. We are not making it harder to do business. We are making it harder to do business unfairly,” EU Commissioner Michael McGrath said in remarks following the DFA draft publication. “We cannot have 21st-century consumers protected by rules that have not kept pace with the 21st-century economy.”
chineseTitle: 战利品盒、影响者和令人上瘾的功能面临欧盟的打击
chineseSummary: 游戏、社交媒体和电子商务平台正面临着新一波全面的欧盟规则，这些规则旨在让“您的在线体验更加公平”。欧盟委员会周三发布的新提议的数字公平法案（DFA）旨在解决利用消费者在网上花费更多时间和金钱的做法，[...]
chineseContent: 游戏、社交媒体和电子商务平台正面临着新一波全面的欧盟规则，这些规则旨在让“您的在线体验更加公平”。欧盟委员会周三公布了新提议的《数字公平法案》(DFA)，旨在解决利用消费者在网上花费更多时间和金钱的做法，包括误导性价格或可用性、游戏战利品盒等令人上瘾的设计功能、未公开的影响者营销等等。欧盟委员会在新闻公报中表示：“该法案将保护所有年龄段的消费者在线购物和浏览商品或服务。” “这也意味着企业竞争更加公平，预计每年可为欧盟消费者节省高达 137 亿欧元（151 亿美元）的费用。”以下是 DFA 提案内容的概述： * 禁止操纵性营销行为和所谓的“黑暗模式”，这些行为会促使消费者做出原本可能不会做出的决定，例如关于产品即将售罄的虚假声明。 * 要求消费者可以选择关闭令人上瘾的功能，例如持续提示、无休止滚动和视频自动播放。令人上瘾的设计的限制也适用于“人工智能伴侣和一般对话聊天机器人”。 * 限制鼓励超支的不公平行为，例如禁止未成年人使用类似赌博的功能（例如付费获胜和付费进步）。 * 要求影响者明确披露广告内容，并限制其利用儿童的信任。 * 限制针对未成年人或利用敏感数据的不公平个性化广告和价格。 * 使订阅和数字合同更容易取消，并提示客户即将到来的
